extracted.intended_audience: immigration attorneys, advocates, researchers, and members of the public tracking asylum rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: Search-results aggregation of Federal Register documents matching the term 'asylum', summarizing proposed rules, final rules, notices, and regulatory excerpts concerning asylum eligibility, credible-fear/reasonable-fear procedures, fees, employment authorization, and related procedural provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: EAD application acceptance pause and waiting period for asylum applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed change to pause acceptance of EAD applications from asylum applicants during periods when affirmative asylum average processing time exceeds 180 days, and to extend the waiting period to apply for employment authorization to 365 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also includes changing EAD application processing time requirements and adding eligibility requirements for EADs based on a pending asylum application (affects filing timing, processing priorities, and when USCIS will accept I-765s from (c)(8) applicants).

rubrics_metrics.name: Asylum and annual pending-asylum fees (HR-1 provisions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Codification of asylum and annual asylum fees, including consequences of non-payment; Section 208(d) expressly authorizes fees for consideration of an asylum application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Noted fee amounts include I-589 initial asylum fee $100 and an Annual Pending Asylum Application Fee $100 per calendar year an I-589 remains pending; the notices indicate when fees take effect, how they are paid (online for some fees), and that some fees have no waiver available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Asylum Officer consideration of certain mandatory bars during credible/reasonable fear screenings
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed and final rules to allow asylum officers (AOs) to consider the potential applicability of certain bars to asylum and statutory withholding of removal during credible fear and reasonable fear screenings, including in screenings where the Circumvention of Lawful Pathways (CLP) rule applies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended to permit earlier identification of persons barred from asylum/withholding; agencies discussed operational flexibility and potential impacts on removal and timeliness of credible fear interviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immigration Judge de novo review must include review of asylum officer's application of bars
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarification that immigration judges' de novo review of asylum officers' credible fear and reasonable fear determinations shall, where relevant, include review of the asylum officer's application of any bars to asylum or withholding of removal under DHS regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a technical amendment to ensure IJ review considers whether AOs correctly applied bars; affects appellate/process review at the credible-fear stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public-health/security-related bars to asylum eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulatory provisions clarifying when an alien who poses a public health risk is ineligible for asylum and withholding of removal (Security Bars rule); these provisions define 'danger to the security of the United States' to include certain emergency public health concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implementation has been delayed and partially withdrawn in places; the rule interacts with credible-fear screening and other asylum-processing rules and has scheduled effective dates that agencies have at times delayed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory standard for granting asylum under INA §208
rubrics_metrics.description: To be granted asylum, eligible noncitizens must satisfy the standards in INA 208 (8 U.S.C. 1158) and also establish that they merit asylum in the exercise of discretion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule text and preambles reiterate that asylum requires both statutory eligibility (e.g., a protected ground and well-founded fear) and a favorable exercise of discretion; DHS/DOJ may set additional limitations and conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpreter requirements for asylum interviews (COVID-19 temporary modification)
rubrics_metrics.description: Temporary modification permitting an applicant for asylum to bring their own interpreter when a contract interpreter is unavailable, to avoid rescheduling and to ensure timely adjudication during the COVID-19 pandemic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule extensions limited in time; when the temporary rule expires, prior interpreter requirements (e.g., reliance on contract interpreters) would again apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form I-589 application content and information-collection requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Form I-589 (Application for Asylum and for Withholding of Removal) is the agency form/collection used to determine whether an alien applying for asylum and/or withholding of removal is classified as a refugee and eligible for relief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notices describe affected public (individuals/households), the information collected, and OMB submission/clearance under the Paperwork Reduction Act; changes to the form or collection must be noticed for public comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Removal of automatic EAD extension practice for renewals
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule amending DHS regulations to end the practice of automatically extending the validity of EADs for aliens who have timely filed an application to renew their EAD in certain categories, to prioritize vetting and screening before issuing a new EAD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Does not affect EADs already automatically extended prior to a specified date or extensions required by law; affects employment authorization continuity and timing for renewal adjudications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appellate timing and procedures for asylum-related appeals to the BIA/EOIR
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative appeals involving consideration of an asylum application must generally be filed within 30 days of a decision granting or denying asylum, or within 30 days of the completion of removal proceedings before an Immigration Judge under section 240, whichever is later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies have issued IFRs to streamline appellate review (e.g., making merits review discretionary in some cases) and to set briefing times; timing rules affect preservation of appellate rights in asylum cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Asylum application in removal proceedings treated as application for statutory withholding
rubrics_metrics.description: An application for asylum submitted by a noncitizen in section 240 removal proceedings is also considered an application for statutory withholding of removal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing an I-589 in removal proceedings preserves consideration for withholding standards even if asylum is denied or inapplicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Circumvention of Lawful Pathways (CLP) as factor in credible-fear screenings
rubrics_metrics.description: Credible fear screenings conducted under circumstances where the CLP rule applies may be affected by the CLP framework; some rulemakings specifically address credible fear screenings in CLP contexts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulations and preambles discuss how CLP interacts with AOs' authority to consider bars and how application of CLP may alter screening outcomes and removal timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: No fee waiver for certain asylum-related fees and specific EAD fees under HR-1
rubrics_metrics.description: The HR-1 mandated fee schedule indicates certain fees (e.g., I-589 initial asylum fee and annual pending-asylum fee) have no fee waiver available; HR-1 also prescribes specific fees for some EAD categories, such as an I-765 initial (c)(8) asylum-applicant EAD fee amount noted in notices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notices provide exact amounts in some instances (e.g., I-589 initial $100; annual pending fee $100; I-765 initial (c)(8) shown as $550 in one notice) and explain payment instructions and waiver availability.

rubrics_metrics.name: EOIR OBBBA fee adjustments applicable to asylum filings
rubrics_metrics.description: EOIR announces inflationary adjustments to OBBBA fees for filings, including fees tied to asylum applications (e.g., $100 for an I-589 and $100 annual pending-asylum application fee), inclusive of statutory OBBBA components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notices list fee tables, effective dates, and how OBBBA fees are incorporated into overall filing costs before EOIR; these adjustments are statutory requirements for fee inflation updates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Serious nonpolitical crime bar (e.g., recruitment/use of child soldiers) as bar to asylum
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulatory items and withdrawn rulemakings refer to bars to asylum based on serious nonpolitical crimes, including specific provisions addressing recruitment or use of child soldiers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some actions concerning such bars have been proposed or withdrawn; these bars operate as categorical ineligibilities for asylum/withholding under statutory/regulatory frameworks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Border referral criteria for credible fear screening
rubrics_metrics.description: If an officer at the border determines an alien indicates an intention to apply for asylum or expresses a fear of persecution or torture, the officer refers the alien to a USCIS asylum officer for a credible fear assessment; if a credible fear is found, the individual may apply for asylum and remain in the U.S. pending final determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This describes the procedural referral and retention standard at the initial inspection stage (INA sec. 235(b)(1)(A)(i)-(iii)); it affects who receives a credible-fear interview and the post-referral processing path.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation and vacatur effects on asylum regulatory text
rubrics_metrics.description: Final rules implementing vacatur remove or reinstate regulatory text governing asylum applications, interviews, and employment authorization eligibility to reflect court vacaturs and subsequent IFRs (i.e., restoring pre-effective-date provisions where appropriate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preambles explain which regulatory provisions are removed or reinserted and how court decisions and successive rulemakings (e.g., Asylum Processing IFR) affect the current regulatory baseline.
